assessment.nobel_worthiness: A persuasive, empirically grounded account of how technology, trade exposure, and task change reshape labour demand and inequality; it has transformed a central public and scientific question.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson provide a coherent core for the task, polarization, and trade-shock contributions.
assessment.maturity: The research program has accumulated extensive evidence, methodological influence, and a durable literature across settings.
uncertainties: The mechanisms of technology and trade are interwoven, so the boundaries of a single cited discovery require careful framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data made intergenerational mobility measurable at unprecedented scale and redirected research toward concrete geographic and policy-relevant determinants of opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are a defensible core for the linked measurement and mobility research program.
assessment.maturity: The data infrastructure, empirical findings, and subsequent research agenda are already highly influential.
uncertainties: The strongest policy interpretations remain more contested than the descriptive measurement contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work established early-life conditions as economically consequential and clarified how health and skill formation generate long-run inequality.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond, and Cunha represent complementary empirical and conceptual strands of the stated contribution.
assessment.maturity: A broad body of quasi-experimental and longitudinal evidence has made early-life economics a durable research field.
uncertainties: The contribution spans several related mechanisms, making a sharply delimited prize citation challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence studies made discrimination visible through transparent field evidence and had major consequences for labour-market research.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are central to the most influential modern audit-study contribution in the proposed group.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been replicated, extended, and incorporated into a substantial evidence base.
uncertainties: Audit studies identify discrimination at particular margins, not every mechanism generating labour-market inequality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM supplied widely used tools for credible empirical analysis when unobserved heterogeneity and endogenous dynamics make simpler methods unreliable.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell, and Bond are closely associated with the central estimators and their development.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been scrutinized over decades and remain foundational throughout applied economics.
uncertainties: Its practical importance is clear, but the contribution may be viewed as narrower and more technical than a discovery with a single substantive application.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed how economists draw credible conclusions when data and assumptions do not justify point identification.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the intellectual anchor, while Tamer and Molinari are important contributors to the modern moment-inequality framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established theoretically and increasingly important in empirical practice.
uncertainties: The broad program has several intellectual branches, and choosing a compact laureate group is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political-economy models linking institutions, political incentives, state capacity, and fiscal outcomes have deeply shaped comparative economic analysis.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini form a particularly clear core, with Besley an important complementary contributor.
assessment.maturity: The body of theory and empirical work has endured and generated a large subsequent literature.
uncertainties: The candidate description encompasses distinct institutional and political-economy research programs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of employer market power corrected a major simplifying assumption in labour economics and altered empirical and policy research on wages.
assessment.attribution: Manning is the principal intellectual figure; Naidu is a strong contributor to the contemporary empirical and conceptual literature.
assessment.maturity: The monopsony perspective is now central to labour-market analysis and has growing empirical support.
uncertainties: The candidate group covers a broad revival rather than one uniquely bounded discovery.
The appropriate allocation of credit among foundational and later contributors remains uncertain.
